## findings

1. **SOURCE-POLICY RED: second reading of the OPR←MEPE prerequisite (C-5).**
   - Symptom: two defensible redemptions. 438.12 for 27541 points with the October run booked first; 480.54 for 30819 points without it.
   - Root cause: the sentence "every point whose expiry month has ended" uses the expiry-month concept of the base clause that MEPE retired. Under MEPE's rule the October run is due today, but October has not ended at 14:10.
   - Evidence: OPR rule; MEPE rule ("A point is aged ... counted in whole months"; "The month-end run is made on the last day of each calendar month"); base service_evt_rewards_points expiry sentence; ledger rows 8d9f6071 (2024-06-15, 3278) and 819aff48 (2026-07).
   - Consequence:
     - The scored credit_amount is 438.12 under one reading and 480.54 under the other.
     - The points argument is 27541 under one reading and 30819 under the other.
     - Booking MEPE after a Reader-B redemption leaves a points balance of −2278.
   - Affected: service.extended.yaml, OPR prerequisite[1].policy_source and rule; gold step 17.
   - First seen in this revision.
2. **SOURCE-FACTOR RED (proof text): computations[EOC].factor_sensitivity[owner_overage_courtesy].tier_taken and computations[PRP].factor_sensitivity[owner_earning_rate].tier_taken name the dealer-arranged tier.**
   - The world takes the outside-lender tier. Evidence: purchase_deals.66b08c97….financing_type = outside_lender, vehicle 0e1d29da (Camry) = the vehicle of labor row f1b34cce.
   - Consequence: the factor-weight proof asserts the customer sits on a tier they do not, which contradicts the trace and the expected values.
   - Affected: tasks/0.json computations[0] and [1].
3. Charter-global, cited, bearing on this tree:
   - C-2: the assembly sentences of EOC, PRP, MEPE and OPR name factor quantities, and the order is load-bearing here (int(4266.25) before +400; courtesies only when overage > 0).
   - C-9: EOC's baseline names "the vehicle".
   - C-1 and C-7(a)(d): no consequence in this world.
4. Observations:
   - The persona line "If the desk tells you some of your points have to stay on the account ... you accept" anticipates the held-points tier. It is passive and conditional, so it is not a defect.
   - The EOC supplies refund applies the 6% labor-based supplies rate to an overage that is mostly parts (391.40 of the 917.72 billed are parts). The rule's "returning the supplies charged on the over-billed work" is therefore not literally true in this world.
